transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-14 14:30 UTC
Duration: ~60 mins
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Acme Head of ML), Carlos Ruiz (Acme Platform), Lina Park (Acme PM)

[00:00] Jordan Lee: hey everyone thanks for joining, um our goal today is to scope the poc and line up latency/throughput slos and a measurement plan. Maya you mentioned chat latency is top KPI?
[00:12] Maya Chen: yeah Jordan, for customer-facing chat we care about time to first token especially — that initial typing feel. Our target is <250ms p95 if possible, p99 under 500ms. but we also need to control per-token throughput so long responses dont explode cost.
[00:25] Priya Rao: right, so we're going to split the SLOs into TTFT (time to first token) and TPOT (time per token) — TTFT covers cold path + network, TPOT is more about model perf and batching.
[00:38] Carlos Ruiz: quick Q: our current infra is Kubernetes on AWS, app tier in us-west-2, we use internal proxy and private subnets, VPC peering for any external inference endpoints is possible but need security review.
[00:50] Jordan Lee: noted. For the poc we'll use Redwood Dedicated sandbox in us-west-2 and can do a VPC peering test. Priya will run benchmarks that mimic your production concurrency.
[01:05] Priya Rao: to set expectations — TTFT measurements are sensitive to network, cold vs warm cache, and model size. For a 13B quantized model on H100-ish infra, typical TTFT p95 we see is ~120-300ms depending on KV cache warm state. TPOT per-token p95 is often 20-40ms with batching tuned.
[01:22] Maya Chen: that sounds reasonable — our median prompt length is around 120 tokens, average generated tokens per response about 80. concurrency spikes to 120 concurrent users during peak.
[01:35] Lina Park: timeline wise we're trying to decide if 2 weeks is enough to sign off a pilot that meets our SLOs and then move to dedicated reserved.
[01:45] Priya Rao: two weeks is typical: week 1 we baseline (replay logs, synthetic load to measure TTFT cold/warm and TPOT), week 2 we iterate (batching, caching, quantization, routing) and run final benchmarks.
[02:01] Carlos Ruiz: for benchmarks we need to know what tooling you'll use and what we'll need to provide. Also need to make sure tests dont trigger rate limit or affect prod.
[02:11] Jordan Lee: we'll use a replay harness plus Fortio/Locust for synthetic concurrency. We'll run against a sandbox endpoint with dedicated capacity; we won't touch prod. We'll provide detailed runbooks and a pre-approved run window.
[02:22] Maya Chen: ok, what's the measurement plan details — how do you capture p95/p99 for TTFT vs TPOT?
[02:30] Priya Rao: measurement plan: 1) Replay: replay anonymized request traces to reproduce real prompt distribution; measure TTFT and per-token timings per request. 2) Synthetic: run controlled concurrency tests varying batch sizes, sequence lengths, and concurrency to map throughput curves and identify knee points. 3) Cold-start tests: restart model worker to measure initial TTFT cold p95/p99. 4) Warm-cache tests: run after priming KV cache. 5) End-to-end network tests: measure from your app tier (we can run an agent in your VPC) to separate network contribution. We'll capture histogram data and compute p50/p90/p95/p99 for both TTFT and TPOT.
[03:10] Maya Chen: and for SLOs we should pick concrete numbers. our initial asks: TTFT p95 < 250ms, p99 < 500ms. TPOT p95 < 35ms, p99 < 80ms. are these realistic?
[03:24] Priya Rao: yes, they're in the expected ballpark for a quantized 13B on H100/4x A100 with batching and KV caching. caveats: if you need strict p99 < 300ms for TTFT with cold starts, that's much harder without pinned warm workers.
[03:39] Jordan Lee: tradeoffs: more pinned capacity reduces cold-start variance and improves TTFT p99 but increases cost. batching improves TPOT but can increase TTFT if you wait to assemble a batch. Redwood Optimize can suggest batching profiles per route to balance both.
[03:55] Carlos Ruiz: we've got strict cost targets — we need to keep tokens/unit costs below a threshold. can we measure cost/latency tradeoff as part of the poc?
[04:04] Priya Rao: yes we'll capture tokens-per-second, cost-proxy metrics (GPU utilization, inference time, and per-token compute) during each run and provide a cost/latency curve so you can choose operating point.
[04:15] Lina Park: any whitespace about model variants? e.g., fallback from a 13B to a 7B for tail requests or fallbacks for region saturations?
[04:24] Priya Rao: absolutely — part of the plan is to test fallback policies and routing. we'll simulate capacity constraints and test automatic fallback to smaller model variants and measure the impact on TTFT/TPOT and quality.
[04:35] Maya Chen: on instrumentation — we need logs and traces for comparison with our APM. can Redwood provide trace hooks and token-level timing?
[04:44] Jordan Lee: yes, Redwood Console exposes per-request token timings, trace IDs, and you can export traces to your tracing backend. we'll include that in the runbook.
[04:53] Carlos Ruiz: security/SSO question: we need SAML and audit logs and key management details before we open peering.
[05:00] Jordan Lee: we'll share SOC2 doc and architecture brief and we can do a short security review call. we'll add that to next steps.
[05:08] Priya Rao: technical detail note: when we measure TTFT we separate network latency (app->gateway), cold worker spinup and model decode start. operationally we record: client-to-gateway RTT, gateway-processing, model-init, first-token-decode. that helps root cause p99 spikes.
[05:25] Maya Chen: good. for our acceptance criteria, can we write it down: 1) TTFT p95 <= 250ms and p99 <= 500ms for baseline prompt distribution in warm state; 2) TPOT p95 <= 35ms and p99 <= 80ms in steady-state with batching; 3) documented cost/latency curve and recommended operating point; 4) validated fallback behavior under saturation.
[05:45] Jordan Lee: sounds good, we'll aim to hit those in the POC. if not, we'll recommend mitigations: pinning workers, increasing reserved capacity, or model quantization changes.
[05:55] Lina Park: final Q on timeline — after the 2-week POC, what deliverables?
[06:01] Jordan Lee: final deliverables: benchmark report (histograms + p50/p90/p95/p99), cost/latency curves, recommended config (batching, cache TTLs, quantization level), security checklist, and a follow-up sign-off session.
[06:15] Maya Chen: ok let's do it. i'll send logs and auth for sandbox.
[06:20] Jordan Lee: great, thanks everyone. recap and next steps in the meeting notes.
